questions.stem: In this developmental scheme, ADA or RAG deficiency (SCID) blocks maturation of BOTH the B and T lineages, whereas BTK deficiency blocks only B cells. Why does the SCID defect affect both lineages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: V(D)J recombination and early lymphoid precursors are shared by both B and T cells, so a defect there halts both

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because it selectively blocks thymic development only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because it impairs BTK signaling downstream of the pre-BCR

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because it prevents immunoglobulin class switching

choices.label: E
choices.text: Because it affects only myeloid progenitors

explanation.summary: RAG enzymes mediate V(D)J recombination required for both BCR and TCR assembly, and ADA deficiency accumulates toxic metabolites that kill developing lymphocytes; either blocks both lineages early, causing SCID. BTK acts later and only in B-cell development.
explanation.whyCorrect: RAG enzymes mediate V(D)J recombination required for both BCR and TCR assembly, and ADA deficiency accumulates toxic metabolites that kill developing lymphocytes; either blocks both lineages early, causing SCID. BTK acts later and only in B-cell development.

questions.stem: BTK deficiency arrests B-cell development at the stage shown, so mature B cells fail to form. What is the characteristic laboratory finding in this X-linked disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated IgE with normal B-cell numbers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absent T cells with normal B cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: High IgM with low IgG and IgA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Absent/very low immunoglobulins of all classes with absent circulating B cells

explanation.summary: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (BTK mutation) blocks the pre-B to immature-B transition, so no mature B cells or plasma cells develop. Patients have absent B cells and panhypogammaglobulinemia, presenting after ~6 months with recurrent pyogenic infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (BTK mutation) blocks the pre-B to immature-B transition, so no mature B cells or plasma cells develop. Patients have absent B cells and panhypogammaglobulinemia, presenting after ~6 months with recurrent pyogenic infections.

questions.stem: A child presents with recurrent skin and soft-tissue abscesses, including these poorly inflamed ('cold') scalp and cutaneous abscesses. This pattern of recurrent staphylococcal abscesses points to a defect in which arm of immunity?

explanation.summary: Recurrent skin and deep-seated staphylococcal abscesses, especially when poorly inflamed, indicate a phagocyte/neutrophil defect in recruitment or microbial killing (e.g., chronic granulomatous disease, hyper-IgE/Job syndrome). Complement defects instead predispose to Neisseria, and T-cell defects to viral/fungal infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Recurrent skin and deep-seated staphylococcal abscesses, especially when poorly inflamed, indicate a phagocyte/neutrophil defect in recruitment or microbial killing (e.g., chronic granulomatous disease, hyper-IgE/Job syndrome). Complement defects instead predispose to Neisseria, and T-cell defects to viral/fungal infection.

questions.stem: This diagram adds MSMD (Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease), which disrupts the IFN-gamma axis between Th1 cells and macrophages. Patients with these defects are especially susceptible to which infections?

explanation.summary: IFN-gamma from Th1 cells activates macrophages to kill intracellular pathogens. Defects in the IL-12/IFN-gamma axis (MSMD) impair control of intracellular organisms, causing disseminated infection with nontuberculous mycobacteria, BCG, and Salmonella.
explanation.whyCorrect: IFN-gamma from Th1 cells activates macrophages to kill intracellular pathogens. Defects in the IL-12/IFN-gamma axis (MSMD) impair control of intracellular organisms, causing disseminated infection with nontuberculous mycobacteria, BCG, and Salmonella.

questions.stem: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), shown here, differs from selective IgA deficiency in that CVID typically involves:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated IgM with defective class switching

choices.label: B
choices.text: Low IgG plus low IgA and/or IgM with poor antibody responses, often presenting in later childhood or adulthood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Isolated low IgA with otherwise normal immunoglobulins

explanation.summary: CVID is characterized by low IgG with low IgA and/or IgM and impaired specific antibody responses, presenting with recurrent sinopulmonary infections, autoimmunity, and increased lymphoma/GI disease risk, typically in the second-to-fourth decades. Selective IgA deficiency involves IgA alone.
explanation.whyCorrect: CVID is characterized by low IgG with low IgA and/or IgM and impaired specific antibody responses, presenting with recurrent sinopulmonary infections, autoimmunity, and increased lymphoma/GI disease risk, typically in the second-to-fourth decades. Selective IgA deficiency involves IgA alone.

questions.stem: These flow plots show a patient with abundant B cells but nearly absent T and NK cells (a T-B+NK- phenotype) from an X-linked defect in the common gamma chain. This shared receptor subunit is required for signaling by which group of cytokines?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21

explanation.summary: X-linked SCID results from mutation of IL2RG, encoding the common gamma chain shared by receptors for IL-2, -4, -7, -9, -15, and -21. Loss of IL-7 signaling blocks T-cell development and loss of IL-15 blocks NK development, while B cells are spared (T-B+NK-).
explanation.whyCorrect: X-linked SCID results from mutation of IL2RG, encoding the common gamma chain shared by receptors for IL-2, -4, -7, -9, -15, and -21. Loss of IL-7 signaling blocks T-cell development and loss of IL-15 blocks NK development, while B cells are spared (T-B+NK-).

questions.stem: This figure contrasts a healthy infant with an infant who has SCID, showing very low or undetectable TRECs in the latter. Why are TRECs reduced in SCID?

choices.label: A
choices.text: TRECs leak out because of a capillary defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: B-cell overgrowth dilutes the TREC signal

choices.label: C
choices.text: TRECs are destroyed by complement in SCID

choices.label: D
choices.text: T-cell production is very low or absent, and TRECs are byproducts of T-cell receptor gene rearrangement in the thymus

choices.label: E
choices.text: The infant produces autoantibodies that consume TRECs

explanation.summary: TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) are DNA circles excised during TCR gene rearrangement and serve as a marker of recent thymic T-cell output. In SCID, thymic T-cell development fails, so TRECs are very low or undetectable, the basis for newborn SCID screening.
explanation.whyCorrect: TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) are DNA circles excised during TCR gene rearrangement and serve as a marker of recent thymic T-cell output. In SCID, thymic T-cell development fails, so TRECs are very low or undetectable, the basis for newborn SCID screening.

questions.stem: One tumor immune-escape mechanism shown is loss of MHC class I so cytotoxic T lymphocytes can no longer recognize the tumor. Which effector cell is best positioned to eliminate such MHC-I-deficient tumor cells?

explanation.summary: Downregulating MHC I evades CTLs but sensitizes the tumor to NK cells, which kill targets lacking inhibitory MHC I. Other escape strategies depicted include tolerization by APCs, antigen modulation, secretion of TGF-beta/IL-10, and creation of an immune-privileged barrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: Downregulating MHC I evades CTLs but sensitizes the tumor to NK cells, which kill targets lacking inhibitory MHC I. Other escape strategies depicted include tolerization by APCs, antigen modulation, secretion of TGF-beta/IL-10, and creation of an immune-privileged barrier.

questions.stem: The oxidative (respiratory) burst diagrammed here is defective in a phagocyte immunodeficiency causing recurrent catalase-positive infections. Which test confirms that diagnosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry (or the nitroblue tetrazolium, NBT, test)

explanation.summary: A defect in the NADPH oxidase that generates superoxide causes chronic granulomatous disease. The DHR and NBT tests measure the phagocyte oxidative burst; failure to oxidize the dye confirms CGD.
explanation.whyCorrect: A defect in the NADPH oxidase that generates superoxide causes chronic granulomatous disease. The DHR and NBT tests measure the phagocyte oxidative burst; failure to oxidize the dye confirms CGD.

questions.stem: The middle panel shows the membrane attack complex lysing a microbe. Deficiency of the terminal components that form this complex (C5-C9) predisposes to infection with which organism?

explanation.summary: The membrane attack complex (C5b-9) is critical for lysing Neisseria, so terminal-complement (C5-C9) deficiencies cause recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal/gonococcal) infections. Other panels show C3b opsonization and C3a/C5a leukocyte recruitment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The membrane attack complex (C5b-9) is critical for lysing Neisseria, so terminal-complement (C5-C9) deficiencies cause recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal/gonococcal) infections. Other panels show C3b opsonization and C3a/C5a leukocyte recruitment.

questions.stem: Red cells shuttle C3b-tagged immune complexes to phagocytes via CR1, as shown. Deficiency of early classical complement components (C1q, C4, C2) impairs this clearance and predisposes to which autoimmune disease?

explanation.summary: Early classical-pathway components opsonize immune complexes with C3b for erythrocyte CR1-mediated transport to the liver and spleen. Their deficiency leads to immune-complex accumulation and is strongly associated with SLE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early classical-pathway components opsonize immune complexes with C3b for erythrocyte CR1-mediated transport to the liver and spleen. Their deficiency leads to immune-complex accumulation and is strongly associated with SLE.

questions.stem: These children share silvery/light hair, partial oculocutaneous hypopigmentation, and a history of recurrent pyogenic infections; their neutrophils contain giant granules. What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Chediak-Higashi syndrome (autosomal recessive LYST mutation) impairs lysosomal trafficking, producing giant granules, partial albinism, recurrent infections, peripheral neuropathy, and a bleeding tendency. Isolated albinism lacks the immunodeficiency and giant granules.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chediak-Higashi syndrome (autosomal recessive LYST mutation) impairs lysosomal trafficking, producing giant granules, partial albinism, recurrent infections, peripheral neuropathy, and a bleeding tendency. Isolated albinism lacks the immunodeficiency and giant granules.

questions.stem: The right image shows a neutrophil with abnormal giant cytoplasmic granules from a patient with Chediak-Higashi syndrome. What underlying cellular defect produces these giant granules?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defective lysosomal trafficking/fusion (LYST mutation) causing failed phagolysosome formation

explanation.summary: Mutation of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) causes granules and lysosomes to fuse into giant dysfunctional structures and impairs phagolysosome formation, so ingested microbes are not efficiently killed, resulting in recurrent infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mutation of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) causes granules and lysosomes to fuse into giant dysfunctional structures and impairs phagolysosome formation, so ingested microbes are not efficiently killed, resulting in recurrent infections.

questions.stem: The neutrophil oxidative burst diagrammed here is absent when NADPH oxidase is deficient (chronic granulomatous disease). Patients are especially prone to infection by which category of organisms?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encapsulated organisms only in the setting of asplenia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Catalase-positive organisms (e.g., S. aureus, Serratia, Nocardia, Aspergillus)

explanation.summary: Catalase-positive microbes degrade their own hydrogen peroxide, so CGD phagocytes lacking NADPH oxidase cannot borrow microbial H2O2 to kill them. Catalase-negative organisms supply peroxide the phagocyte can still use.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catalase-positive microbes degrade their own hydrogen peroxide, so CGD phagocytes lacking NADPH oxidase cannot borrow microbial H2O2 to kill them. Catalase-negative organisms supply peroxide the phagocyte can still use.

questions.stem: This lung biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation; the inset silver stain reveals septate hyphae branching at acute (~45-degree) angles. What organism is this, a classic cause of infection in chronic granulomatous disease?

explanation.summary: Septate hyphae with acute-angle (~45-degree) dichotomous branching are characteristic of Aspergillus, and invasive aspergillosis is a hallmark infection in chronic granulomatous disease. Mucormycosis instead shows broad, ribbon-like, nonseptate hyphae with wide-angle branching.
explanation.whyCorrect: Septate hyphae with acute-angle (~45-degree) dichotomous branching are characteristic of Aspergillus, and invasive aspergillosis is a hallmark infection in chronic granulomatous disease. Mucormycosis instead shows broad, ribbon-like, nonseptate hyphae with wide-angle branching.

questions.stem: This assay compares oxidative burst (measured by flow cytometry and a colorimetric slide reaction) in resting versus PMA-stimulated neutrophils from a normal subject, an affected patient, and a carrier. The affected patient's neutrophils fail to show the stimulation-induced signal shift. A defect in which enzyme complex best explains this result?

explanation.summary: The figure shows a dihydrorhodamine (DHR)/flow-cytometry respiratory burst assay. Normal neutrophils shift dramatically with PMA (SI ~139), while the affected patient (XL-CGD) shows almost no shift (SI ~1.2) and the X-linked carrier shows a bimodal population. Failure to generate the oxidative burst reflects a defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase, the hallmark of chronic granulomatous disease. Myeloperoxidase deficiency still permits the burst; LYST defects cause Chediak-Higashi; the others are unrelated to this assay.
explanation.whyCorrect: The figure shows a dihydrorhodamine (DHR)/flow-cytometry respiratory burst assay. Normal neutrophils shift dramatically with PMA (SI ~139), while the affected patient (XL-CGD) shows almost no shift (SI ~1.2) and the X-linked carrier shows a bimodal population. Failure to generate the oxidative burst reflects a defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase, the hallmark of chronic granulomatous disease. Myeloperoxidase deficiency still permits the burst; LYST defects cause Chediak-Higashi; the others are unrelated to this assay.

questions.stem: This flow-cytometry histogram measures cell-surface expression of a leukocyte molecule. The patient's cells (compared to negative control and to both parents) show markedly reduced expression, while both parents express it normally. Given the near-absent expression demonstrated here, which condition does this patient most likely have?

explanation.summary: The histogram measures CD18, the beta-2 integrin subunit. The patient's leukocytes essentially lack CD18 expression while both heterozygous parents express it normally, consistent with autosomal recessive leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1. Without CD18, neutrophils cannot firmly adhere to and cross the endothelium, producing recurrent infections without pus. CGD is a defect of the oxidative burst, not CD18 expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: The histogram measures CD18, the beta-2 integrin subunit. The patient's leukocytes essentially lack CD18 expression while both heterozygous parents express it normally, consistent with autosomal recessive leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1. Without CD18, neutrophils cannot firmly adhere to and cross the endothelium, producing recurrent infections without pus. CGD is a defect of the oxidative burst, not CD18 expression.
